description: A harmless fly in bee's colours — the adults are steady pollinators, while the aphid-eating larvae of many species quietly keep pests in check. Tell it from a bee by its single pair of wings and the hovering flight.

description: Ohio's great yellow butterfly — four black tiger stripes and tailed hindwings, its caterpillars feeding on tree leaves like cherry and tuliptree while the adults drift widely for flower nectar. Females come in a yellow form and a dark form thought to mimic the toxic pipevine swallowtail.

shelter: Winters in the mountains of central Mexico
description: The orange-and-black butterfly of milkweed and September skies — its caterpillars eat only milkweed, its adults nectar widely, and the last generation of the year flies from Ohio to the mountains of Mexico to spend the winter.

shelter: Overwinters as a pupa in a leaf shelter
description: Ohio's largest and most familiar skipper — a fast, chunky brown butterfly with a gold band across the forewing and a bright silver-white patch under the hindwing, raised on honey locust and other legumes and drawn to purple and pink flowers.

shelter: Overwinters as eggs in bark and twigs
description: The voice of Ohio's summer nights — a leaf-green insect that lives high in the oak canopy, rarely flies, and rasps its two-syllable 'ka-ty-did' from dusk to dawn from midsummer until the first hard frost.

shelter: Nymphs live 2–5 years on tree roots underground
description: The buzz of August heat — a heavy green-and-black insect with clear wings whose males drone from the treetops on the hottest afternoons, after years spent underground as nymphs drinking from tree roots.

shelter: Overwinters as egg pods in the soil
description: Ohio's most common grasshopper — an olive-and-yellow leaper with red hind shins that grazes meadow grasses and forbs from midsummer to frost, and in doing so feeds the kestrels, meadowlarks, bluebirds, and turkeys of open country.

shelter: Flies south in fall; few overwinter in Ohio
description: The orange-and-black bug of the milkweed pods — a seed-feeder that drinks from developing milkweed seeds through the pod wall, gathers in bright clusters of nymphs and adults, and wears the plant's own toxins as a warning. Harmless to monarchs and to the plant.
